slides.heading: Reverse Polish Notation
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Stacks
slides.narration: Let's solve Reverse Polish Notation, a medium stacks problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Evaluate postfix tokens with + - * / (integer division truncating toward zero).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Evaluate postfix tokens with plus - / (integer division truncating toward zero).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Operands go on a stack; each operator pops two and pushes the result.
slides.narration: Operands go on a stack; each operator pops two and pushes the result.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Build an expression tree then evaluate → extra structure
Stack evaluation → O(n) time and space
slides.narration: You could build an expression tree, but a single stack is enough: numbers are pushed, operators pop two and push the result.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. On an operator, pop right then left
slides.narration: Step by step. First, push numbers. Second, on an operator, pop right then left. Third, apply and push. Fourth, return the last value.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: Operator +: pop 17 and 3, compute 3 + 17 = 20, push it.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: Operator -: pop 2 and 20, compute 20 - 2 = 18, push it.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: Operator /: pop 18 and 50, compute 50 / 18 = 2, push it.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each token: plus and times push the result of two pops; minus and divide pop b first then compute a op b; anything else is parsed and pushed. Return the final pop.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Operand order for − and /: second pop is the left operand
slides.narration: For minus and divide, the first pop is the right operand. Division truncates toward zero.

slides.narration: A follow-up converts infix to RPN with the shunting-yard algorithm.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Operands go on a stack; each operator pops two and pushes the result.
slides.narration: To recap Reverse Polish Notation: Operands go on a stack; each operator pops two and pushes the result. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
